sources.title: Pregel: A System for Large-Scale Graph Processing (Malewicz et al., 2010)

structure.rationale: The book follows a progressive skill-building arc: motivation (ch1), conceptual foundations (ch2), first hands-on build (ch3), then layered power features — state/memory (ch4), control flow (ch5), multi-agent (ch6) — before production concerns (ch7) and a capstone case study (ch8). The appendix bridges LangChain users. This mirrors LangGraph's own learning curve: simple graphs first, then cycles, then agents.
structure.audience: Python developers with basic LLM experience (have used ChatGPT API or LangChain) who want to build stateful, production-grade AI workflows. No prior LangGraph experience assumed.

claims.text: LangGraph is a low-level orchestration framework for building stateful agents
Inspired by Google's Pregel and Apache Beam, with interfaces influenced by NetworkX
Production/Stable status, MIT license, Python >=3.10
Current version 1.2.x, trusted by Klarna, Replit, Elastic

pitfalls: LangGraph is not a replacement for LangChain — it orchestrates, LangChain provides components

claims.text: StateGraph is a generic builder class: StateGraph(Generic[StateT, ContextT, InputT, OutputT])
Nodes are functions that take state and return partial state updates
State keys can use Annotated[type, reducer] for aggregation across nodes
START and END are reserved constants for entry and exit points

pitfalls: StateGraph is a builder and cannot be used directly — must call .compile() first

claims.text: MessagesState provides a prebuilt state with messages key and add_messages reducer
ToolNode and tools_condition are prebuilt components for tool-calling agents
graph.get_graph().draw_mermaid() generates a Mermaid diagram of the graph

pitfalls: API keys must be set as environment variables before graph invocation

claims.text: MemorySaver is an in-memory checkpointer for development; SqliteSaver/PostgresSaver for production
thread_id in config isolates conversations
Store provides cross-thread long-term memory with namespace-based organization

pitfalls: MemorySaver loses state on process restart — use persistent checkpointers in production

claims.text: interrupt_before/interrupt_after in compile() pauses execution at specified nodes
interrupt() function provides dynamic interrupts from inside nodes
graph.get_state_history(config) enables time-travel debugging

pitfalls: Interrupt requires a checkpointer — without one, the graph cannot resume

claims.text: Compiled graphs can be added as nodes in a parent graph (subgraphs)
Send() API enables dynamic fan-out to parallel nodes
create_react_agent provides a one-liner for building tool-calling agents

pitfalls: State schemas must be carefully mapped between parent and child graphs

claims.text: Streaming modes: values, updates, messages, events, custom
LangSmith integration provides tracing, visualization, and debugging
RetryPolicy supports max_attempts, initial_interval, backoff_factor
LangGraph Platform (Cloud or self-hosted) for scalable deployment

pitfalls: Streaming mode 'messages' only works with LLM calls that support streaming

claims.text: LangGraph can orchestrate complex pipelines with conditional error recovery loops
Pydantic models can be used for structured LLM output in graph nodes

pitfalls: Generated Cypher must be sanitized — use read-only transactions and query limits

claims.text: LangChain provides components (models, tools, retrievers); LangGraph provides orchestration
LangChain's Runnable interface is compatible with LangGraph nodes

pitfalls: Not everything needs LangGraph — simple chains are better served by LangChain's LCEL

volatile: LangGraph version numbers and API surface — the library is actively developed
LangGraph Platform pricing and deployment options
Prebuilt component names (ToolNode, tools_condition, create_react_agent) may change
